item.title: Chase Adds Qantas, Cathay Pacific as Transfer Partners
item.description:
Source: NerdWallet
Chase has added Qantas Frequent Flyer and Cathay Pacific Asia Miles as transfer partners, effective Nov. 18, 2026. This expands Chase’s transfer partner list to 16 programs, including 12 airlines and four hotel loyalty programs. Points from Chase Ultimate Rewards® transfer at a 1:1 ratio to the new partners. Eligible cards include the Chase Sapphire Reserve® and Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card. The additions enhance award availability for flights on Qantas and Cathay Pacific, which are Oneworld alliance carriers. Award seats are typically more available through airline loyalty programs, making Chase points valuable for routes like Cathay Pacific’s Aria Suite business class or Qantas’ upcoming Sydney-London route. While existing transferable currencies like Capital One miles offer similar benefits, Chase users can gain more redemption opportunities with these new partners. Welcome offers on select cards remain the best way to earn Chase points.

item.title: What makes Americans feel financially ready to have kids? It’s complicated.
item.description:
Source: Vox
The 2026 American Family Survey, conducted by Brigham Young University and YouGov, found that Americans' financial readiness to have kids is more tied to their financial trajectory than current income. Among childless adults under 50, 44% of those whose finances improved over the past year said they definitely want children, compared to 24% of those whose finances worsened. Income had a smaller impact: 29% of earners under $50,000 and 32% of those earning $100,000 or more expressed strong desire for kids. Andrew Cherlin noted that financial direction, not current income, shapes future perceptions. Young adults prioritized financial stability, careers, and housing before having children, with higher earners listing more conditions. Jeremy Pope emphasized that people care about security but define it differently. Persistent financial hardships, rising childcare costs, and economic uncertainty are deterring some from feeling ready. Policies like affordable housing, childcare support, and paid family leave could help. The survey also revealed that 42% of respondents faced serious financial hardships this year, up from 35% in 2025, with lower-income groups most affected. Melissa Kearney noted that relationships, not just money, influence family formation decisions for some young adults.

item.title: Ukraine Considers Ceding Donetsk for NATO Membership
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Would Ukraine trade land for NATO membership or protection?
The US has asked Ukraine whether it would cede Donetsk province to Russia in exchange for NATO membership. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated no concrete proposal has been made and emphasized he cannot decide unilaterally, stressing any agreement would not recognize Russia's occupation. The US envisions bilateral security guarantees akin to those with Israel, similar to Articles 4 and 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, though without U.S. troops. Experts like Oleksandr Kraiev criticize the land-for-security idea, calling it a flawed diplomatic approach and warning of a 'second Budapest Memorandum.' A Kyiv International Institute of Sociology survey found 61% of respondents reject ceding Ukrainian-controlled Donbas territories, while 35% would accept a land-for-security deal. Analysts argue such a deal would violate Ukraine's constitution and set a dangerous precedent. Alternatives include a security arrangement modeled on West Germany's NATO membership before reunification, with Kyiv's territory protected only under its control. Sergiy Solodkyy called the proposed deal a 'trap' orchestrated by Russia and U.S. negotiators.

item.title: Seven local hospitals see downgrades in latest Leapfrog Group safety report
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune
Seven hospitals in the region received lower safety grades in the latest Leapfrog Group report. UC San Diego’s La Jolla, Hillcrest, and College Area campuses dropped from A to B, while Scripps Memorial Hospital La Jolla fell from B to C. Palomar Health’s Escondido and Poway hospitals also saw single-grade drops. Two hospitals, Kaiser Permanente’s San Marcos and Sharp Chula Vista, improved to A. No San Diego County hospital scored below a C. Nationally, 900 As, 655 Bs, 655 Cs, 35 Ds, and three Fs were awarded. Leapfrog combines government data and hospital surveys to rate performance across 32 measures. Patient infection rates, particularly blood infections at Naval Medical Center and UCSD Hillcrest, and surgical site infections at multiple facilities, drove the worst results. UCSD Health stated corrective actions were already underway, citing ongoing quality surveillance. Scripps Health noted pandemic-era data influenced its La Jolla score, which was 0.04 points from a B. Naval Medical Center did not comment. Hospital safety grades are publicly available at hospitalsafetygrade.org.

item.title: San Diego Delays Reserve Target to 2041 Amid Funding Shortfall
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: San Diego again softens its reserve policy despite rainy day fund being more than $150M below target
San Diego officials delayed achieving its rainy day fund target from 2030 to 2041 after reserves fell $150 million below the 16.67% goal. The new plan requires annual contributions of 0.5% of operating revenues ($10 million) and sets a 10% reserve floor to maintain credit ratings. City finance officials argue the slower approach avoids budget cuts to libraries and programs, but independent analyst Charles Modica doubts its feasibility, citing reliance on rare revenue windfalls. Councilmember Vivian Moreno criticized the plan as irresponsible, warning of financial risks. The policy would prevent skipping contributions without declaring an economic downturn. Credit ratings impact bond rates, crucial for infrastructure financing. The changes take effect in 2029 after eliminating a $300 million budget deficit. Councilmember Kent Lee questioned whether lowering the target is better than maintaining it with no realistic pathway. The policy also removes an unused pension reserve and strengthens liability reserves.

item.title: Emergency repairs to begin on Bayshore Bikeway in Imperial Beach
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego
The Port of San Diego will begin emergency repairs on the Bayshore Bikeway in Imperial Beach due to erosion and damage from recent water level surges linked to El Niño and Kelvin waves. Work is set to start mid-November and last 15 to 20 days, with periodic partial closures of the bikeway. Contractors will implement traffic control measures, flaggers, and advance warning signs to ensure cyclist safety. Repairs will include temporary erosion prevention, debris removal, de-watering, culvert rehabilitation, headwall reinforcement, and embankment reconstruction. The project aims to stabilize the structure, protect infrastructure, and maintain public access until permanent improvements are completed. Officials emphasized the need for caution as the work progresses.

item.title: Mortgage Rates Drop to 7.13% Today
item.description:
Source: NerdWallet Original headline: Mortgage Rates Today, Wednesday, November 18: Moving Lower
Mortgage rates fell to 7.13% APR today, down 21 basis points from yesterday but up 13 basis points from a week ago. The 30-year fixed-rate average reflects mixed inflation data, with October’s Producer Price Index showing 0.3% monthly inflation versus 0.4% expected, and 6.5% year-over-year growth—the highest in four years. Analysts expect the Federal Reserve to raise the federal funds rate in December, likely pushing mortgage rates higher. Homeowners with rates above 7.63% may consider refinancing, though breaking even on closing costs requires staying in the home long enough. Lenders adjust rates daily based on market conditions, so personalized quotes can change until locked. Borrowers are advised to preapprove, compare offers, and use affordability calculators to assess monthly payments. Rate locks protect against increases during loan processing, especially with market volatility.

item.title: IAEA chief reports North Korea expanded uranium enrichment plant
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: North Korea expanded uranium enrichment plant, says IAEA head
IAEA chief Rafael Grossi reported North Korea has expanded its uranium-enrichment plant at Yongbyon. The IAEA, unable to access North Korea since 2009, relies on satellite imagery to monitor nuclear activity. Grossi confirmed construction of a new extension to the Yongbyon facility began in mid-September 2026, with external completion by late October 2026. He called the expansion 'a cause for serious concern.' Enriched uranium can power reactors or nuclear weapons. North Korea's nuclear program faces international sanctions but has continued development. In September 2024, North Korea revealed its first covert uranium plant. Kim Yo Jong, Kim Jong Un's sister, defended the country's nuclear status as 'absolute,' dismissing calls for denuclearization. The IAEA passed resolutions in September 2024 addressing North Korea's nuclear program. Kim Jong Un has repeatedly criticized U.S. policies, linking nuclear weapons to self-defense against South Korea and the U.S.

item.title: San Diego School District Approves Electric Bike Safety Policy
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Distrito Escolar Unificado de San Diego aprueba una política de seguridad para bicicletas eléctricas
The San Diego Unified School District approved a new electric bike safety policy, effective January 5, following a unanimous board vote. The policy emphasizes education, free permits, and safety guidelines for students using electric bikes on campus. Superintendent Fabiola Bagula stated the policy prioritizes student well-being, promoting safe and responsible bike use. The policy includes safety training, parental verification, and designated parking areas. Dr. Howard Taras highlighted a 33% quarterly rise in injuries from electric bikes over three years, urging the policy to mitigate risks. Students will have 60 days to comply before full implementation on March 8. Ethan Ramirez, a student board member, praised the policy for fostering informed, responsible users. The policy aims to enhance road safety for students and the broader community.

item.title: Muslims to outnumber Christians by 2035, research shows
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle
Pew Research Center projects Muslims will outnumber Christians globally by 2035. The study attributes this to higher fertility rates among Muslim women, who average 3.1 children between 2020-2025 compared to 2.5 for Christian women. By 2035, Muslim populations are expected to reach 2.57 billion, surpassing Christians at 2.52 billion. Projections show Muslims could exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, while Christians may fall short of 3 billion. The U.S. will no longer be a Christian majority by 2070, though Christians will remain the largest group. Sub-Saharan Africa will host over half the world’s Christians, with the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpassing the U.S. as the country with the most Christians. Pakistan, India, Nigeria, and Indonesia will lead Muslim populations. Hindus will grow fastest outside India, while China, Japan, and South Korea face shrinking populations. Europe’s Christian numbers will drop 35.8%, while its Muslim population will rise to 13%. Pew researchers note growth is not at Christians’ expense, with most expansion occurring in majority-religion countries. Experts emphasize inter-religious education to address demographic shifts.

item.title: San Diego Port Raises Waterfront Parking Rates Amid Inflation
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego, San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: San Diego Port Increases Waterfront Parking Rates Amid Inflation Concerns
The Port of San Diego approved a $1 hourly parking rate increase for the North Embarcadero corridor, effective Jan. 4, 2027. Rates will rise from $2.50 to $3.50 per hour, with enforcement hours extended to 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. The change applies to meters and lots in areas like the USS Midway Museum and Star of India. Officials cited 49% inflation over the past decade as a key factor, though rates remain below regional market levels. The adjustment aims to fund 23 public parks, Harbor Police, and environmental programs. Juneteenth was added to free parking holidays. The port expects an additional $1 million in annual revenue. Critics like Laura McClanathan and Bashir Alenadaaf questioned the necessity, while CEO Scott Chadwick defended the move as essential for operations. Commissioner Danielle Moore raised affordability concerns, urging a lower rate cap. The board approved a district-wide rate range up to $3.50, though they opted for a lower cap at Moore’s request. Timothy Rosario, a visitor, acknowledged the cost but said it wouldn’t deter future visits.
item.source: ABC 10News San Diego, San Diego Union-Tribune

item.title: 20 US metros with longest commutes ranked by 2025 Census data
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: The 20 US metros with the longest commutes to work, ranked
The Census Bureau's 2025 American Community Survey data ranks the 20 US metros with the longest travel times to work. The average one-way commute in the US was 27.4 minutes, up from 27.2 minutes in 2024 and 26.8 minutes in 2023. Factors include RTO mandates pushing workers back to offices and increased distances due to pandemic-era housing shifts. The top metros include Lexington Park, Maryland, with a 39.4-minute average commute, and New York-Newark-Jersey City at 36.8 minutes. Public transportation use varies, with New York having 28.2% transit commuters and Lexington Park reporting only 0.8%. Most workers drove alone, with percentages ranging from 63.7% in Bridgeport to 78.4% in Lexington Park. Carpooling rates also differ, with Riverside-San Bernardino-Ontario at 12% and Hagerstown-Martinsburg at 10.2%. The data includes workers aged 16+ who did not work from home, with 87% reporting commuting to a workplace.

item.title: P-8 Crews Hunt Submarines Amid Challenging Conditions
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: How P-8 crews hunt submarines through long hours, low flying, and a sea of underwater noise
Royal Air Force P-8 Poseidon crews conducted a 10-hour anti-submarine exercise in the Baltic Sea during Dynamic Merlin, a NATO drill simulating a hunt for a Swedish submarine. The mission involved navigating rough weather, deploying 130 sonobuoys to detect underwater noise, and using radar and acoustic sensors to track the target. Crews faced challenges like distinguishing submarine sounds from merchant vessels and managing vast search areas. The Baltic's shallow waters and variable salinity complicate sonar effectiveness, allowing submarines to detect surface ships at greater ranges. A simulated torpedo strike, coordinated with a Swedish helicopter, concluded the exercise after delays caused by poor weather. The P-8's role in NATO's anti-submarine efforts highlights the need to counter Russian naval activity. Crews endure long hours and mental strain, with one operator noting the task's difficulty without the aid of alcohol. The exercise underscores the importance of training in complex environments to prepare for operations in the North Atlantic.

item.title: Hyatt Introduces Milestone Rewards, Delta Partnership Benefits
item.description:
Source: NerdWallet Original headline: World of Hyatt Adds Milestone Rewards, New Delta Benefits
Hyatt introduces Milestone Rewards and expands Delta partnership benefits. The new program allows stacking of awards like Free Night Certificates and Suite Upgrades on single stays, with a 365-day expiration for all awards. Laurie Blair, Hyatt's senior vice president, emphasized member preferences for more personalized benefits. Globalist members will no longer receive automatic free parking; instead, they can choose it as a Milestone Reward. Delta and Hyatt elites can earn points in both programs, with Hyatt elites needing premium Delta tickets for points. Milestone Rewards start at 10 nights or 20,000 points, offering tier credits, spa credits, and new options like Delta eCertificates. Award expiration dates are now standardized. Hyatt and Delta members can link accounts for bonus points, with promotions including tier credits and sweepstakes entries. Globalists grandfathered into free parking until February 2028. Booking systems now allow combining awards on single stays, and account linking is encouraged for upcoming promotions.

item.title: Comedian Katt Williams treats rejection as a numbers game
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Comedian Katt Williams says his career rule is to treat rejection as a numbers game: 'How many nos equal a yes?'
Comedian Katt Williams describes rejection as a numbers game, stating that success depends on calculating how many 'nos' lead to a 'yes.' On the 'IMO' podcast, Williams explained he determined that 300 rejections equate to one acceptance, prompting him to contact 900 people daily to secure three sales. He emphasized that rejection is necessary for progress, noting that America's strength comes from people striving to excel at their jobs. Williams, 55, began his career in the 1980s and is known for his role in 'Friday After Next.' Film producer William Packer shared that Beyoncé rejected his movie five times before agreeing to star in 'Obsessed,' using her feedback to refine the script. Alisa Wood, now a KKR partner, kept a rejection letter from Henry Kravis and later joined the firm after another partner invited her to interview. Both examples underscore the value of persistence in the face of rejection.

item.title: L.A. County Issues Evacuation Warnings Amid Storm Threat
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: L.A. County issues evacuation warnings as storm nears; snow, flooding expected
L.A. County issues evacuation warnings as a major atmospheric river storm approaches, bringing rain, snow, and flooding. The National Weather Service forecasts widespread rain, gusty winds, and mountain snow, with rainfall rates up to 0.75 to 1 inch per hour. Flood watches are in effect for Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, Ventura, and Los Angeles counties, except the Antelope Valley. Evacuation orders target residents near burn scars from recent wildfires, including areas affected by the Eaton, Palisades, Sunset, Kenneth, Hurst, and Canyon fires. Authorities urge residents to avoid flood-prone zones like canyons and waterways. The storm, linked to a strong El Niño, could deliver 1 to 3 inches of rain, with coastal slopes seeing 3 to 5 inches. California’s State Operations Center is coordinating resources, including prepositioned fire equipment and swift water rescue teams. Northern California also faces impacts, with flooded roads, power outages, and closed highways. Snowfall of 4 to 8 inches is expected above 7,000 feet in the Sierra, bolstering the state’s snowpack, which provides 30% of its water supply. Additional storms and high surf advisories remain in effect through Friday.

item.title: Del Mar Council Approves 29th Street Seawall Project Contract
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Del Mar council approves contract for 29th Street project
Del Mar City Council voted unanimously Nov. 10 to approve a conceptual design for the 29th Street Seawall and Beach Access Project and related contracts. The city will spend $125,784 on approved contracts and task orders. The project aims to improve the seawall and public beach access, addressing deficiencies like limited emergency vehicle access and a wooden stairway over the seawall. ENGEO was previously contracted for the conceptual design in two phases, with a future phase including stairs north of the proposed ramp. However, construction cannot proceed until the neighboring property owner completes noncompliant seawall improvements and removes riprap obstructing the stairway. The property owner declined to coordinate, citing readiness issues. Staff anticipates 1 to 1.5 years for final design, permitting, and bidding before construction begins.

item.title: Fast-moving storm hits San Diego County on Thursday
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Una tormenta de rápido desplazamiento azotará partes del condado de San Diego este jueves
A fast-moving storm from the northwest will bring up to 0.5 inches of rain to northern San Diego County and similar amounts in some southern areas on Thursday. The system is expected to arrive in the north around 11 a.m., spreading southward within an hour, with most moisture dissipating by evening. Scattered showers may occur on Friday and Saturday. Winds up to 48 km/h could disrupt traffic on Interstate 8 east of Alpine. A storm warning remains for beaches until Friday morning due to waves 1.2-1.8 meters high, potentially reaching 2.4 meters, causing major beach flooding and minor inland inundation. The National Weather Service warns of possible rain on Thanksgiving and notes El Niño-driven tides could exceed 2.4 meters (8 feet).

item.title: Sunset Cliffs Parking Lot and Trail Closed After Seawall Collapse
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Parking lot, trail at Sunset Cliffs closed due to partial seawall collapse
A parking lot and trail along Sunset Cliffs Boulevard were closed this week after a section of the seawall collapsed due to erosion and damage from powerful surf, high tides, and rain. Officials confirmed the collapse occurred over the weekend, with photos showing a large open section of the structure from base to near the top. Closures between Adair and Osprey streets will remain until crews assess damage and stabilize the bluff. Signage warns visitors of the danger. A rainstorm forecast for Thursday could further impact cliff stability. Officials noted coastal erosion is accelerated by high tides, wave activity, rising sea levels, and El Niño events, which intensify flooding, wave size, and erosion. The seawall protects the bluff from wave action.

item.title: Ukraine's Allies Meet in Berlin to Coordinate Support Amid War
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Ukraine's allies gather in Berlin for 'Coalition of the Willing' summit
Ukraine's allies meet in Berlin for 'Coalition of the Willing' talks as leaders from Germany, France, the UK, Poland, and Italy gather with NATO head Mark Rutte and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy emphasized priorities including air defense, energy support, and diplomatic efforts to end the war. Ukraine claimed responsibility for a third attack on the Kerch Bridge, using Neptune missiles to disrupt Russian supply lines. Prince Harry stated he would rejoin military service to fight Russia if needed. The UK pledged 1,000 long-range strike drones worth £260 million to Ukraine ahead of winter. German Foreign Minister Wadephul called for a clear signal to Russia, stressing allies' readiness for all outcomes, including military support. The meeting coincides with Trump's talks with Putin and Xi Jinping, aiming to coordinate responses to potential developments. The coalition seeks to demonstrate unity in securing legal security guarantees for Ukraine.

item.title: William and Kate Meet PM Modi During India Visit
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: William and Kate meet PM Modi as they wrap up India tour
Prince William and Princess Catherine met India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi during their three-day visit. Modi thanked William for bringing the Earthshot Prize to India, where the couple awarded £1m to environmental winners. Catherine visited a maternity hospital, comforting a grieving mother who lost a baby. The royals discussed UK-India relations, emphasizing strengthened partnerships for shared prosperity. Modi called the meeting a 'pleasure' and expressed hope for future collaboration. William highlighted India's climate leadership as reason for hosting the Earthshot Prize in Mumbai. The couple last met Modi in 2016. Catherine visited Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, where she spoke with Jyoti Karande, a mother of premature twins. The visit combined diplomacy with personal projects, reflecting their role as UK diplomatic assets. Catherine, recovering from cancer treatment, resumed international duties.

item.title: Chula Vista Councilmember Demands Release of Union Charter Records
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Chula Vista council member seeks release of records tied to failed union-drafted charter package
Chula Vista Councilmember Jose Preciado demanded public release of all communications and documents related to a failed union-drafted charter amendment package. The 13-part proposal, submitted by LIUNA in June, would have raised council salaries, extended term limits, and mandated binding arbitration for police and fire disputes. The council voted 4-1 in July to remove it from the ballot after critics argued it bypassed standard review processes. Preciado’s request followed federal agents searching LIUNA official Kelvin Barrios’ home, with Barrios denying allegations of political influence. Campaign filings show LIUNA spent over $158,000 supporting candidates. Preciado urged full disclosure, including closed-session discussions, while Mayor John McCann supported transparency but cautioned against releasing sensitive materials. City Attorney Marco Verdugo noted closed-session waivers would require separate agenda items. Preciado emphasized the need for public access to all communications involving Barrios or the charter package.

item.title: AWS Exec Uses AI Agent to Plan Daily Outfits
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: AWS's Matt Wood has an AI agent help plan his outfit every day
AWS chief AI and technology officer Matt Wood uses an AI agent to plan his daily outfits. The agent, part of AWS Quick, checks his calendar around 4 a.m. to identify the day's most important meeting and suggests a dress code. Wood said he avoids overdressing and prefers to wait until after his first coffee to decide what to wear. The AI also activates a smart light bulb in his closet, flashing colors like red for keynotes or blue for team meetings. Clothes in his closet are color-coded, allowing him to quickly select matching items. Wood noted the system helps him avoid decision fatigue, saying 'no thought necessary.' Beyond outfit planning, he uses AI to scan overnight news reports, prepare for meetings, and develop ideas. He mentioned processing nearly a billion tokens in AI usage this week. The unconventional use of AI has drawn attention from Amazon employees.

item.title: Xi Jinping Engages in Diplomatic Outreach at APEC Summit
item.description:
Source: FP Foreign Policy Original headline: Xi Plays the Field at APEC Summit
Chinese President Xi Jinping engaged in diplomatic outreach during the APEC summit in Shenzhen, meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump. Xi emphasized a multipolar world and criticized trade protectionism, while Trump received a high-profile welcome including an honor guard and military flyover. Their trilateral summit will address Russia-Ukraine, Iran, and nuclear disarmament, though experts expect Xi to avoid nuclear collaboration. Meanwhile, Iran launched strikes on a U.S. base in Kuwait, escalating tensions. The EU proposed a $49.5 billion loan to Ukraine to address its funding gap, though some member states oppose it. South Korea introduced AI cheating restrictions for its university entrance exam after a student used AI to secure a high score. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. surprised Trump with a Jollibee chicken delivery during his Asia tour.

item.title: Anthropic Employees Can Swap Shares for Luxury Homes
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Anthropic workers can swap their shares for these 3 homes. Getting to the office is another question.
Anthropic employees can trade equity for luxury homes as the company prepares for its IPO. Three properties are listed for exchange: a $29.995 million Los Angeles mansion with a five-hour commute to the nearest office, a $6.25 million Tribeca apartment within walking distance of a new NYC office, and a $5.99 million Brooklyn home offering Manhattan views. Sellers cite market conditions and AI industry optimism as reasons for accepting shares. Phillip Braunstein, owner of the LA mansion, noted the local luxury market is soft but expects Anthropic shares to appreciate over time. He uses AI for personal tasks, including bill payments. Sebastian Sagar, who listed his Tribeca apartment, cut the price and switched brokers. A Brooklyn seller added Anthropic shares as payment option after learning of the IPO filing, framing the home as a commuter's choice between transit or scenic views.

item.title: Santa Monica Man Found Dead Was Air Force Vet and Background Actor
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Man found dead near Santa Monica Pier was 'multifaceted' Air Force vet, background actor, family says
A 38-year-old background actor, Alexander Haskin, was found dead in the ocean near Santa Monica Pier on Monday. Police confirmed no evidence of an altercation, with initial findings indicating no suspicious circumstances. His cause of death remains pending further investigation. Haskin, who lived alone in Los Angeles Chinatown, was identified as a background actor in Netflix’s 'You' and ABC’s 'The Rookie.' His father, Dana Haskin, described him as a 'multifaceted guy' with interests in music, fitness, fishing, day trading, and acting. Haskin served in the U.S. Air Force Security Forces before becoming a personal trainer and later pursuing acting. He last spoke with his father on Saturday, appearing in good spirits and planning to spend Thanksgiving with family. Security footage confirmed he was alone before the incident. Authorities urge witnesses to contact Santa Monica Police Department at 310-458-8491.

item.title: 27-Year-Old Man Killed in Vista Vehicle Collision
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Man, 27, struck by vehicle and killed in Vista
A 27-year-old man was killed after being struck by a vehicle while running across East Bobier Drive in Vista. Sheriff's deputies responded to the collision around 7 p.m. Tuesday, arriving to find the man already deceased despite bystander aid. Investigators said two men were running northbound when a westbound vehicle attempted to avoid a collision but struck one of them. The driver remained at the scene, called 911, and was later released. Authorities ruled out alcohol or drug involvement. Tips about the incident are requested via the sheriff's Vista station or Crime Stoppers. Copyright 2026, City News Service, Inc.

item.title: Luckey Warns of Tech Outages, Urges 3 Days of Supplies
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Palmer Luckey on tech outages: ‘Everyone should have 3 days of water’
Palmer Luckey, Anduril cofounder, urged during a global tech outage surge that everyone should stockpile three days of water and dry food. Speaking at The New York Times DealBook summit, he linked the outages to rushed AI-driven updates creating vulnerabilities. Outages affected Microsoft Outlook, FAA communications, and NSA networks, though US officials denied cyberattack links. Sen. Mark Warner suggested the disruptions stemmed from security efforts, not malicious activity. VP JD Vance canceled a DealBook appearance to address the outages. Luckey speculated that AI tools enabled exploits, prompting outdated systems to adopt countermeasures. He emphasized three-day resilience as critical, stating the US could restore systems within that timeframe. Luckey, known for doomsday prepping, owns missile bases for storing his video game collection.

item.title: Third Death Linked to Six Flags X2 Roller Coaster
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Third death is reportedly linked to a high-speed roller coaster at a California Six Flags amusement park
Christopher Gibson, 17, died June 4 after riding the X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain. An autopsy found he suffered blunt force head trauma from a large subdural hemorrhage. Gibson and his mother visited the park for his high school graduation, riding multiple coasters including X2 twice within four days. He left with a headache after the second ride and died later that evening. His death occurred weeks before two others suffered severe brain injuries on X2 in July. Naomi Greer-Wilkinson and Pamela Guillen were treated for brain hemorrhages after riding the coaster. Magic Mountain closed X2 on July 12 following an investigation and announced its permanent retirement on Sept. 29. Six Flags stated the ride passed safety tests for nearly 20 years. A CNN investigation linked X2 to two deaths and over a dozen serious injuries since 2002. A 2024 lawsuit by the Hawley family, alleging the ride was unreasonably dangerous, was settled before trial without admitting fault. Hilda Farias died in 2010 from a brain rupture allegedly caused by X2, with her family’s case settled for an undisclosed amount.

item.title: Fast-moving storm to bring rain to San Diego County Thursday
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Fast-moving storm to drench parts of San Diego County on Thursday
A fast-moving storm from the northwest will bring up to half an inch of rain to North County and nearly that amount to parts of South County on Thursday. The system is expected to reach North County around 11 a.m., spreading southward within an hour. Most rain should dissipate by nightfall, though sporadic showers may occur Friday and Saturday. Winds up to 30 mph could complicate driving on Interstate 8 east of Alpine. A beach hazard advisory remains in effect until late Friday morning due to heavy surf, with waves reaching 4-6 feet and possibly 8 feet, leading to minor flooding. Forecasters note El Niño-enhanced tides may result in wetter conditions around Thanksgiving.

item.title: ABC 10News Gifts Free Books to San Diego Kindergartners
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: ABC 10News brings free books and a love of reading to Oak Park Elementary kindergartners in San Diego
ABC 10News visited Oak Park Elementary School to provide free books to kindergartners as part of its Storytime initiative. Morning Anchor Jared Aarons read to students, emphasizing the importance of fostering a love for reading. Teachers noted many students lack personal books at home, relying on shared resources from siblings. Each child selected five books to take home and received an unexpected sixth. Kindergartner Aaron expressed excitement, stating the books would help him learn more. Teachers highlighted reading's role in subjects like math and science, encouraging students to embrace challenges. The program is funded by donations, North Island Credit Union, the Scripps Howard Fund, and the San Diego Council on Literacy. Teachers stressed the value of reading in building lifelong skills and appreciation.

item.title: Helicopter Crash in Florida Linked to Low Altitude Flight
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Helicopter that crashed in Florida, killing 1 and injuring 2, was flying ‘extremely’ low, NTSB says
A helicopter crashed in Biscayne Bay on Nov. 4, killing the pilot and injuring a photographer and videographer. The National Transportation Safety Board reported the aircraft was flying extremely low, with rotor blades striking water during a turn. The Robinson R44 II was filming a powerboating event when it hit the water, causing the crash. Some doors were removed to facilitate filming. The photographer described the helicopter flying low parallel to a boat’s side before turning for a shot, leading to the collision. TV footage showed the helicopter upside down underwater with emergency floats attached. Witnesses made distress calls, and a good Samaritan assisted an injured person. Multiple agencies, including the Coast Guard and Customs and Border Protection, responded to the crash site.

item.title: Multiple Service Outages Spark Speculation on Cybersecurity Threats
item.description:
Source: The Atlantic Original headline: What on Earth Is Going On?
Multiple major service outages disrupted Microsoft Outlook, U.S. air traffic, major banks, United Airlines, Apple services, and a National Security Agency network within a week. Public speculation focused on AI, cybersecurity threats, or hostile actors, though officials like Secretary of State Marco Rubio dismissed cyberattack theories. Nicole Perlroth suggested rapid network updates might have caused cascading issues, though companies blamed technical glitches. The FAA grounded flights due to a networking equipment failure, while banks faced limited account access disruptions. Analysts debated whether these events were isolated or part of a broader pattern, with some noting the frequency illusion amplifies perceived connections. The author questioned the public’s expectation of constant system reliability and highlighted media literacy concerns, citing misleading social media content and outdated weather reports. Despite investigations, no conclusive link between incidents was found, leaving uncertainty about the true cause.

item.title: Kobey's Swap Meet faces uncertain future as Midway Rising project moves forward
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Kobey's Swap Meet faces uncertain future as Midway Rising project moves forward in San Diego
Midway Rising project threatens Kobey's Swap Meet's future. The development plan includes shops, apartments, and an entertainment center across 48-49 acres. Anthony Pretto, vice president of Operations, inherited the role from his parents and has led the swap meet since 1980. He fears the project will displace the long-standing market, which serves thousands of San Diegans. Pretto expressed concern over his daughters' potential loss of the community space, saying, 'I don't know what's going to happen.' Over 2,000 people have signed a petition urging city support. Pretto's current lease expires at year's end, and he's negotiating an interim lease with Pechanga Arena. He acknowledged change is inevitable but emphasized adaptation. City officials have not yet responded to requests for support of iconic businesses like Kobey's.

item.title: Ukraine's Underground Pipeline Front Line Evades Drones
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: 'The drones don't fly here' - BBC reports from Ukraine's new front line
Ukrainian forces are fighting Russian troops in an underground Soviet gas pipeline in Kharkiv region, avoiding drone attacks and artillery. The tunnel, called the Kupyansk metro, is used to transport troops and supplies via an electric cart. Soldiers describe the subterranean battlefield as cramped, dangerous, and psychologically taxing, with frequent encounters and boobytrapped barriers. Operation Veles, named after a Slavic underworld god, has advanced 15km (9.3 miles) since April 2025. Ukrainian troops, including Colombian volunteers, face risks like ricochets, suffocation, and panic attacks. Russian forces also use the pipeline for infiltration, leading to ongoing clashes. Zanuda, a Ukrainian planner, calls this the 'only option' as surface operations are nearly impossible. The operation has retaken territory and boosted morale but hasn't altered the war's trajectory. Ukrainian President Zelensky praised the success, though challenges remain as both sides continue to exploit the pipeline's strategic value.

item.title: Hollywood Veteran Uses AI to Create Satirical Tech Videos
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: AI is helping this Hollywood veteran make videos that would never have existed before
Ari Kuschnir, a Hollywood veteran with a background in commercial filmmaking, is using AI to create satirical videos mocking tech executives. His AI-generated content, posted on YouTube and X, features tech leaders in absurd scenarios presented as 1980s infomercials or crime dramas. Kuschnir previously required a $200,000 budget and weeks of work for similar projects, but now produces videos in six to eight hours with $1,000 in direct costs. He emphasizes that AI allows him to focus on storytelling, humor, and editing rather than production logistics. After selling his production company in 2021 and relocating following a Los Angeles fire, Kuschnir has rediscovered creative freedom through AI tools like Seedance, which help generate scripts and visuals. He distinguishes his work from AI-generated remixes of existing shows, arguing his content creates original characters and formats. Kuschnir warns that over-reliance on AI could degrade quality but believes it enables new creative possibilities. 'We just got the keys to the imagination castle,' he said.

item.title: Paramedic's Son Dies in Garage Accident She Responded To
item.description:
Source: ABC News: Top Stories Original headline: Paramedic responding to deadly accident discovers son is the victim
Logan Mumford, 28, died after a car he was working on collapsed on him in Sigurd, Utah. His mother, Tricia Mumford, a paramedic, responded to the scene and later realized the victim was her son. The accident occurred Monday evening when Mumford, helping a neighbor fix a car, attempted to access the alternator. A car jack 'suddenly gave way,' trapping him beneath the vehicle. Deputies and first responders, including his mother, worked to free him, but he suffered severe head trauma. Mumford was airlifted to Utah Valley Medical Center, where he died from his injuries. Authorities noted the personal tragedy for the family, emphasizing the emotional impact on first responders. Mumford, a father of two young children, was described as someone who 'always willing to lend a hand and help others.' The Sevier County Emergency Management highlighted the community's grief, stating the incident became 'far too personal for one of our own.'

item.title: U.S. Catholic bishops launch AI task force for regulation and worker protections
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: US Catholic bishops’ new AI task force urges regulation and worker protections
U.S. Catholic bishops have launched an AI task force to advocate for regulation and worker protections as technology advances. Following Pope Leo’s encyclical 'Magnifica Humanitas,' which called for AI oversight, Bishop Oscar Cantú of San Jose emphasized the Church’s role in safeguarding human dignity. The task force, chaired by Cantú, will lobby lawmakers for 'clear guardrails' on AI development and monitor labor impacts. Bishops also approved updated investing guidelines prohibiting investments in AI technologies that fail to protect human dignity. The task force aims to address youth AI use, promote AI literacy, and support displaced workers. Archbishop Paul Coakley framed AI as 'a faint reflection of human intelligence' created in God’s image. Bioethics professor Charles Camosy, an advisor, highlighted healthcare ethics in AI use. The bishops, while acknowledging limited tech expertise, are rapidly learning and collaborating with industry leaders to shape ethical AI practices. The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB) also pledged to protect children from online exploitation and support automation-displaced workers.
